title: Choose the visual world for decklume's website
question: The roll assigned the Light Table. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Light Table
options.lineage: slide-projector light tables, 35mm mounts and Carousel trays
options.thesis: Your deck as mounted slides on a glowing light table: pick, inspect with a loupe, project.
options.viewport: A dim studio desk with one wide glowing light table: real slides in numbered mounts, one under a loupe, the headline set on the table edge, the install command typed on a mount label.
options.risk: The literal reading of the name; turns skeuomorphic if mounts are over-rendered.

raised.raise: Chrome stays achromatic; colour lives only in the slides, so the ten themes are the page's palette.
The deck runs as one unbroken mount strip with a live 'now projecting' marker; it scales, never wraps.
Every mount carries a catalogue number (DL-01…) that doubles as site-wide wayfinding.
The projector beam is built for real (canvas light with drifting dust), not painted.
One calm panel holds the install action; everything around it may be dense.
The glow commits as one continuous horizontal field across the viewport.

options.label: The Contact Sheet
options.lineage: photographers' contact sheets and grease-pencil edits
options.thesis: Every deck printed as a contact sheet; grease-pencil circles choose the frame.
options.viewport: A full-width contact sheet of real slides in film strips, the chosen frame circled, the headline written in the margin.
options.risk: Familiar from photo portfolios; most runs in a visual-review category land near it.

options.label: Step Sequencer
options.thesis: Slides as sixteen lit step keys under a chase light.
options.viewport: A step row of slides with a running chase light.
options.case: Fuses poorly: students and teachers don't read their talks as drum patterns.
options.risk: Gimmick for anyone who doesn't make music.
options.kept: One unbroken sequence with a live 'now' marker.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A breathing shader field with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: Full-screen shader, one oversized word, tiny corner links.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hides the slides and reads as the AI-startup look you ruled out.
options.risk: Slow on school laptops; offer becomes opaque.
options.kept: Build the signature technique for real, not as a picture.

options.label: Fly-posted Flyer
options.thesis: Every inch occupied, one calm ticket panel on top.
options.viewport: Collage plane with a white finder card floating on it.
options.case: Fuses poorly: busy and childish, both ruled out by you.
options.kept: One calm panel holds the action amid density.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything gets a catalogue number; colour codes replace words.
options.viewport: Vast black, one pulse plot, a small catalogue number.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded labels fight first-time clarity.
options.risk: Too cryptic for students arriving from search.
options.kept: A strict catalogue numbering used as wayfinding.

options.label: Indoor Sun
options.thesis: One amber hall, a half sun, silhouettes on the floor.
options.viewport: A long amber horizon band with a half disc.
options.case: Fuses poorly: amber flattens the ten themes' colours, the product's proof.
options.kept: One continuous field committed across the viewport.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: Achromatic field; colour only at hairline edges.
options.viewport: Wide white margins, thin humanist type, colour fringes.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too quiet to make a deck tool desirable.
options.risk: Reads as documentation, which you ruled out.
options.kept: Chrome stays achromatic so colour belongs to the work.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A developer-tool landing executed impeccably: headline, install command, feature grid, screenshots.
canonCard.viewport: Centred headline and install command over a screenshot, features in a grid below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other skill or dev tool by design.
